rulings.evidence: REUSE of the live board id `adobo-seasoning` (4 of 7, cheapest 0.1332 at Sam's Club) - only the vocabulary row is missing, which is a naming question and not a registrar one, per the brown-lentils precedent. REFUSED Chipotle in Adobo: canned peppers in sauce are a different food from a dry salt-and-garlic blend.

A cubano is built with deli-sliced ham, so this is exactly what deli-ham prices (7 of 7). The 'spiral ham' ruling refused deli-ham for a bone-in whole ham; that argument runs the other way here. REFUSED Diced Ham - a convenience pack, different form and price. 8 slices at 28 g (1 oz sandwich slice).

Cooked seasoned pulled pork shoulder; board reports no commodity and no capture match, and no vocabulary row shares a core word. New id proposed. Weighed from the USDA household measure, 1 cup = 135 g, not guessed.
REUSE of the live `pickles` id (7 of 7, cheapest 0.05 at Sam's Club); the vocabulary just has no plain-form name row. Long sandwich-cut slices weighed at 15 g each.

REFUSED the board's `sliced-cheese` match: that generic prices processed sandwich singles, a different food and a much lower price class than swiss. Slicing is a cut of the same cheese, so the vocabulary's own Swiss Cheese [swiss-cheese] row holds. 12 packaged slices at 21 g.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Cooked, seasoned, shredded pork shoulder, sold refrigerated in tubs (Del Real, Kirkland) or made from a pork butt. 945 g at batch scale, so a major component and not a garnish. The pre-resolve table reports the board carries NO commodity and NO capture match for it, and no vocabulary row shares a core word. It is not any existing pork id I can see evidence of: deli-ham, diced-ham and spiral-ham are cured ham at different price classes, and the run's own pork-loin protein is a different, much leaner cut sold raw. If the estate already prices this food under another spelling - pulled-pork, pork-carnitas, pork-shoulder or pork-butt - alias it rather than minting a duplicate; a pork-shoulder alias is the likeliest correct answer and I would accept it, since the cooked yield is about 65% of raw.
